name: Posture Botox / muscle relaxants

lead: Botulinum toxin injected into neck or shoulder muscles is discussed as a way to ease tension. Botulinum toxin is established for conditions such as cervical dystonia and muscle spasticity.
No trial found tests it for posture correction or appearance in otherwise healthy people.

paras: The toxin blocks acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction, causing temporary muscle weakness that reverses as nerves regenerate.

Adverse effects include spread to unintended muscles, weakness, swallowing trouble and allergic reactions, and the US FDA added boxed warnings about toxin spread in 2009. It is prescription-only in the US, UK, Canada, Australia and EU.

trials.title: Quantifying Musical Performance After Treatment With Myobloc in Musician's Dystonia

lead: Posture Botox refers to the use of botulinum toxin injections in neck or trapezius muscles for tension. Botulinum toxin is an acetylcholine release inhibitor that causes flaccid paralysis of the injected muscle, with the effect slowly reversing as the nerve regenerates.[1]

Its established medical uses include cervical dystonia, with type B approved by the FDA in 2000, and other muscle spasticity and spasm conditions; the Wikipedia article does not list trapezius or general neck tension as a specific indication.[1] Many therapeutic uses are off-label in the US.[1]
No study identified has tested botulinum toxin for improving posture or appearance in healthy people.

paras: Botulinum toxin is used for spasticity in cerebral palsy, stroke and spinal cord injury, cervical dystonia, chronic migraine prophylaxis (FDA-approved 2010) and other conditions.[1] Cosmetic use, mainly for glabellar lines, was FDA-approved in 2002.[1]
Spread of toxin can cause weakness of unintended muscles, trouble swallowing, headaches, flu-like symptoms and allergic reactions, and the FDA added boxed warnings about toxin spread in 2009.[1]
No studies found for posture or appearance use. A registered trial of a different botulinum toxin product studied musicians with focal dystonia, a separate condition.[2]

timeline.event: Type B toxin approved for cervical dystonia.[1]
FDA approves cosmetic use for glabellar lines.[1]
FDA adds boxed warnings about toxin spread.[1]
